object.label: Cellatlas can run universal preprocessing with a single command.
Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data
object.description: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. Existing workflows are often assay-specific, while read structures, barcode correction, and UMI/read counting differ across RNA, ATAC, protein, tags, and spatial modalities. cellatlas uses machine-readable seqspec files to configure modular tools for uniform preprocessing across nine datasets, modalities, and single-cell technologies.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: These universal principles guided our development of cellatlas for universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data. The cellatlas program requires sequencing reads, genomic references, and a seqspec specification file. From there, cellatlas leverages seqspec functionality to auto generate the kallisto technology string that specifies the 0-index position of the cellular barcodes, molecular barcodes, and genomic features such as cDNA or genomic DNA. It also either points to, or generates, a barcode onlist compatible with the barcodes in the FASTQ files. Thus, cellatlas can be used to process data with a single command: cellatlas build -o out -m rna -s spec.yaml -fb bcs.txt -fa genome.fa -g genome.gtf R1.fastq.gz R2.fastq.gz

object.description: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: Uniform preprocessing makes it straightforward to compare modalities within the same technology. Figure 2 shows a comparison of data from three different DOGMA-seq (Mimitou et al. 2021) modalities as assayed in (Z. Xu et al. 2022), all preprocessed with cellatlas and the tools it uses: snATAK, kallisto bustools, and kITE. Uniform preprocessing also allows for quantifying the efficiency of assaying the different modalities. The fact that the RNA and protein libraries have a similar number of UMIs captured for a given number of reads (Figure 2a,b) is consistent with similar dilutions of the libraries (1.99nM and 2.2nM respectively), whereas the tag library efficiency (Figure 2c) is distinctly different, likely as a result of dilution to 0.27nM. While the exact cause for the difference requires further investigation, the control for preprocessing that cellatlas provides points to an experimental cause for the difference. Uniform preprocessing also provides a direct comparison of the distinct modalities in terms of their detection efficiency (Figures 2d,e,f). The protein detection saturates because DOGMA-seq protein modality only assayed 163 proteins. The discrepancy between cells in which protein is detected but not ATAC peaks, versus those in which protein is detected but not RNA, is interesting and warrants further investigation.

object.label: Voyager: exploratory single-cell genomics data analysis with geospatial statistics
object.description: Spatial organization is central to tissue function, and exploratory spatial data analysis can reveal structure in single-cell genomics data. Decades of geospatial methods have not been fully adapted to standard spatial-omics workflows. Voyager provides local, bivariate, and multivariate spatial methods through a common interface, a geometry-aware data structure, reproducible tutorials, and consistent R and Python implementations, revealing signals such as biologically relevant negative spatial autocorrelation.

object.label: Design principles for open source bioinstrumentation: the poseidon syringe pump system as an example
object.description: Rapidly changing single-cell genomics benefits from adaptable laboratory hardware, while shared open designs can keep instrument developers from starting from scratch. Open bioinstruments still need concrete design guidance to remain functional, robust, simple, modular, benchmarked, and documented. Poseidon demonstrates these principles with a customizable syringe-pump and microscope system that costs under $400, assembles in under an hour, and performs microfluidic experiments.

object.label: Reliable and accurate diagnostics from highly multiplexed sequencing assays
object.description: Scalable, inexpensive, and secure SARS-CoV-2 testing is crucial for pandemic control, and highly multiplexed sequencing assays are promising alternatives to RT-qPCR tests. Their clinical use requires reliable analysis, interpretation, and computational workflows that handle sample indices, biological targets, gene counts, and infection-status classification. A kallisto-bustools workflow processes recently proposed sequencing-based diagnostic tests quickly and with low memory, validates SwabSeq analysis against an orthogonal workflow, and extends to assays with different targets and sample-index structures.

object.label: Pseudoalignment facilitates assignment of error-prone Ultima Genomics reads
object.description: Lower sequencing costs could broaden biological and clinical projects, but new platforms must still yield assignable reads. Ultima Genomics single-cell RNA-seq reads show elevated errors in and near homopolymers and lower quality than matched Illumina reads. Pseudoalignment compensates for these errors and assigns Ultima reads better than standard read alignment.

object.label: Quantifying orthogonal barcodes for sequence census assays
object.description: Barcode-based sequence census assays can label biological features, but barcode design and technical noise complicate quantification. Assay-specific tools can be slow, memory-intensive, and hard to standardize across multimodal, multiplexing, and perturbation assays. kITE uniformly quantifies orthogonal barcode assays with fast, memory-efficient kallisto-bustools processing, while qcbc evaluates barcode-set quality and identifies ambiguity from shared subsequences, homopolymers, and low-diversity designs.

object.label: Quantifying orthogonal barcodes for sequence census assays
object.description: Orthogonal barcodes encode biological and technical information across multimodal, multiplexing, and perturbation assays.
